cancer_indication: Advanced or metastatic hormone receptor–positive (HR+) breast cancer (typically HER2–), especially after progression on other endocrine therapy.
moa: Fulvestrant competitively binds estrogen receptor α (ERα), blocking estrogen binding and triggering receptor ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. As a pure antiestrogen with no agonist activity, it causes complete shutdown of ER signaling. In ER+ breast cancer cells, this leads to G1 cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. Its clinical effect is often combined with targeted agents such as CDK4/6 inhibitors or a PI3K inhibitor for synergistic benefit.

GOBP_ESTROGEN_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Estrogen receptor–driven signaling and transcriptional programs mediated by ERα (ESR1) (and to a lesser extent ERβ/ESR2) that promote luminal breast cancer growth.
GOBP_ESTROGEN_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: ER-driven transcription is the core dependency in HR+ breast cancer that fulvestrant targets by degrading ERα and shutting down estrogen-responsive gene expression.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth and survival signaling that can be hyperactivated in HR+ breast cancer (e.g., via PIK3CA mutations).
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: This pathway provides pro-survival signaling and reduced dependence on ER signaling, contributing to endocrine resistance in breast cancer.

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: ErbB/HER family receptor signaling (including HER2/ERBB2, ERBB3, ERBB4, and EGFR) that can drive proliferation and survival.
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Growth factor receptor signaling can bypass ER blockade; ERBB-family upregulation is described as a resistance mechanism in the setting of endocrine blockade.

KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: MAPK/ERK signaling downstream of growth factor receptors that sustains proliferative signaling.
KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: MAPK/ERK activity can maintain proliferation and is described as increased in fulvestrant-resistant contexts.

BIOCARTA_NFKB_PATHWAY.description: NF-κB survival signaling that drives anti-apoptotic gene expression in tumor cells.
BIOCARTA_NFKB_PATHWAY.interpretation: Active NF-κB is associated with survival/resistance, while its suppression is described as important for fulvestrant-induced apoptosis.

REACTOME_GPER1_SIGNALING.description: GPER1 (GPR30) signaling as an alternate membrane estrogen receptor pathway that can persist during fulvestrant treatment.
REACTOME_GPER1_SIGNALING.interpretation: Loss of GPER1 signaling is described as associated with fulvestrant resistance; GPER1-mediated signaling may represent a potential resistance route during treatment.

GOBP_CELL_CYCLE_G1_S_PHASE_TRANSITION.description: Regulatory processes controlling G1 cell-cycle arrest and progression through the G1/S checkpoint, including Cyclin D–CDK4/6 and RB/E2F control noted in the source.
GOBP_CELL_CYCLE_G1_S_PHASE_TRANSITION.interpretation: Fulvestrant efficacy is linked to inducing G1 arrest; upregulation of G1/S drivers (e.g., Cyclin D/CDK6 activity) is described as a mechanism that can overcome ER blockade.

GOCC_RB_E2F_COMPLEX.description: RB/E2F control referenced as governing E2F target gene expression and the G1 checkpoint in breast cancer cells.
GOCC_RB_E2F_COMPLEX.interpretation: RB1 loss/downregulation is described as abrogating fulvestrant-induced G1 arrest, enabling unchecked proliferation despite ER loss.

REACTOME_INTERFERON_GAMMA_SIGNALING.description: IFNγ-driven signaling through STAT1 and IRF1 described as an immune/stress axis that can influence tumor apoptosis programs.
REACTOME_INTERFERON_GAMMA_SIGNALING.interpretation: Activation of IFNγ–STAT1–IRF1 signaling is described as sensitizing breast cancer cells to fulvestrant by suppressing survival programs and promoting caspase-dependent apoptosis.

REACTOME_APOPTOSIS.description: Apoptotic signaling described as caspase-dependent apoptosis activated as fulvestrant takes effect.
REACTOME_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptosis pathway activation is described as enhancing fulvestrant antitumor effect, particularly in ER+ tumor cells.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High expression of ER target genes is described as indicating robust ER signaling, which predicts good fulvestrant response.
High expression of ER target genes is described as indicating robust ER signaling, which predicts good fulvestrant response.
IFNγ induces STAT1 as part of an IFNγ–STAT1–IRF1 axis described to restore fulvestrant sensitivity by promoting apoptotic signaling and suppressing survival programs.
IRF1 induction is described to suppress NF-κB/BCL2 and trigger caspase-dependent apoptosis, restoring fulvestrant sensitivity.
Upregulation of pro-apoptotic BAX is described as part of IFNγ-driven restoration of fulvestrant sensitivity through apoptosis.
Upregulation of pro-apoptotic BAK1 (BAK) is described as part of IFNγ-driven restoration of fulvestrant sensitivity through apoptosis.
Upregulation of caspase-dependent apoptosis (including caspase 8) is described as amplifying fulvestrant-induced cell death and enhancing drug effect.
Upregulation of caspase-dependent apoptosis (including caspase 9) is described as amplifying fulvestrant-induced cell death and enhancing drug effect.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Suppression of BCL2 (described as part of IFNγ/IRF1 effects) is linked to enabling caspase-dependent apoptosis and restoring fulvestrant sensitivity.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PIK3CA mutations are described to hyperactivate PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling, driving survival and reduced dependence on ER signaling, leading to fulvestrant resistance.
Upregulation/overexpression of HER2 (ERBB2) is described as a bypass mechanism that can render fulvestrant ineffective in resistant contexts.
ERBB3 expression is described as increased with endocrine blockade in ER+ contexts and as part of ErbB-family bypass signaling linked to fulvestrant resistance.
ERBB4 expression is described as increased with fulvestrant/endocrine blockade in ER+ contexts, contributing to compensatory ErbB signaling.
EGFR is described as part of ErbB-family signaling that can be upregulated and provide alternate mitogenic drive despite ER inhibition.
CDK6 overexpression is described to drive G1/S progression despite ER loss, mediating resistance to fulvestrant.
Cyclin D1 amplification/upregulation is described as a cell-cycle driver that can push cells through G1/S regardless of ER blockade, contributing to resistance.
Activating ESR1 mutations (e.g., Y537S, D538G) are described as emerging in endocrine-resistant metastatic tumors and reducing fulvestrant efficacy.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss/downregulation of GPER1 signaling is described as associated with fulvestrant resistance.
Loss of RB1 (E2F control) is described as abrogating fulvestrant-induced G1 arrest, permitting unchecked proliferation and resistance.
Downregulation of STAT1 is described as detrimental because STAT1 is part of IFNγ–STAT1–IRF1 signaling needed to trigger fulvestrant-induced apoptosis.
Downregulation of IRF1 is described as detrimental because IRF1 suppresses NF-κB/BCL2 and is required for caspase-dependent apoptosis linked to fulvestrant effect.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B): Clinical data confirm fulvestrant’s benefit is confined to ER+ (Luminal) tumors. In HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B) metastatic cancer, fulvestrant demonstrates efficacy similar to aromatase inhibitors; the FALCON trial showed longer PFS with fulvestrant vs anastrozole in previously untreated HR+/HER2– cases.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive: HER2+ tumors (HER2-enriched or Luminal B with HER2 amplification) are often endocrine-resistant and typically require combined HER2 blockade; fulvestrant is not used as monotherapy in HER2+ disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative/basal-like: Triple-negative/basal-like tumors (virtually all ER–) lack ERα and do not respond to fulvestrant.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-mutated or “HRD+”: BRCA1/2-mutated or “HRD+” cancers are treated with DNA-damage agents, not fulvestrant; only if they co-express ER would fulvestrant be considered.
